chandamama_rave.title: చందమామ రావే
chandamama_rave.meaning: A classic Telugu rhyme calling out to the moon (Chandamama/Jabilli), asking it to climb over the hill and bring a shower of flowers — sung to soothe and delight young children.

vaana_vaana.title: వానా వానా వల్లప్పా
vaana_vaana.meaning: A short, playful rhyme children chant when it rains, noticing the rainwater collecting right at the doorstep.

nidrapo_nidrapo.title: నిద్రపో నిద్రపో
nidrapo_nidrapo.meaning: A gentle jola paata (lullaby) pattern sung to put babies to sleep — the child's own name is traditionally sung in place of 'Ramachandra'.

jojo_laali.title: జోజో లాలి
jojo_laali.meaning: Another common jola paata (lullaby) refrain — 'jo jo' is a soothing sound used across many Telugu lullabies to gently rock a baby to sleep.

chitti_chilakamma.title: చిట్టి చిలకమ్మ
chitti_chilakamma.meaning: A gentle, affectionate rhyme addressing a pet parrot as 'little parrot' — a common opening used in children's rhymes and stories featuring a parrot character.

bomma_borusu.title: బొమ్మ బొమ్మ బొరుసు
bomma_borusu.meaning: The traditional call Telugu children use when flipping a coin to make a choice — 'bomma' (the image side) or 'borusu' (the plain side), just like calling 'heads or tails' in English.
